Need recent form.As of October 10, 2026, José Mourinho is Real Madrid's manager, about two months into his second spell, and nothing suggests he is about to leave. If things stay as they are, the question would resolve **Yes**.

**The Metaculus source:** I couldn't load the linked question (metaculus.com/questions/45857), so I can't say what it currently shows. It opened October 6, 2026. To resolve Yes, Mourinho must stay in charge without a break until 12:00 UTC on December 31, 2026.

**Appointment and contract**
- On June 11, 2026, Real Madrid signed Mourinho to a three-year deal running until June 30, 2029.
- His appointment became inevitable after President Florentino Pérez was re-elected that week. Pérez made Mourinho one of the core pillars of his reelection campaign, so the president is personally tied to this hire. That points toward patience.
- Madrid paid Benfica €15 million in compensation to release him, and he replaced Álvaro Arbeloa.
- He took over after back-to-back trophyless seasons under Carlo Ancelotti, then Xabi Alonso and Arbeloa.

**Results so far**
- His first game was August 22, a last-gasp 2-1 win at Espanyol.
- Around September 16, after a 3-2 win at Elche, Madrid had five wins and one loss for 15 points. The loss was 1-0 to Betis.
- Their last match before the international break was a 2-1 defeat away to Atlético. Madrid are now 4th in LaLiga, 5-0-2, 15 points.
- Goal.com calls it a relatively faltering start, but also notes no new injuries by mid-October, which hasn't happened in the past ten years.
- I didn't find Champions League results.
- Media mood is mostly fine. ESPN, for example, ran a piece headlined "Will Real Madrid's title hopes be over before El Clásico?" I saw no reports of board unrest or a crisis in the dressing room. His most visible problem is Vinícius struggling.

**Upcoming fixtures that could matter**
- Today, Oct 10: Villarreal at home (round 8). Madrid are the betting favourites.
- Oct 18: Sevilla at home.
- Oct 21: RB Leipzig at home (Champions League).
- Oct 25: Barcelona away (El Clásico).
- November and December bring more league and Champions League group matches. I don't have exact dates for those. Real Madrid also usually plays the Supercopa in January, which is after the deadline.

**Base rates (from my own knowledge, not checked against sources)**
- Under Pérez, Madrid has sometimes fired a manager mid-season:
  - Lopetegui was sacked in October 2018, about four months in, after a heavy Clásico defeat.
  - Benítez was sacked in January 2016.
  - Alonso left in January 2026.
- Most Pérez managers, though, have made it through their first December.
- Generally, the chance of an elite-club manager being sacked within any roughly 2.7-month window is low, maybe 5–10%. It's higher at Madrid, and higher when results are bad.
- Mourinho has never been sacked this early into a job. His dismissals usually come in his second or third season (Chelsea 2007 and 2015, Man United 2018, Tottenham 2021).
- Other ways he could leave: health problems (he is 63), or resigning in a clash with players or the president.

**Prediction markets:** I didn't find any market on this.

razonamientos:
(a) **Time left:** About 82 days, until 12:00 UTC on December 31, 2026.

(b) **Status quo:** Mourinho is currently Real Madrid’s manager. If nothing changes, the answer is Yes.

(c) **Reference class:** As a rough base rate, most elite-club managers still in post in October remain through December—perhaps 85–90%. Madrid’s readiness to make mid-season changes makes this case somewhat riskier.

(d) **No scenario:** A run of poor results, especially around El Clásico or in the Champions League, prompts Madrid to replace him before the deadline.

(e) **Yes scenario:** Results remain adequate, and the club gives its recently appointed, three-year-contract manager at least the rest of 2026.

(f) **Technicality:** He must remain manager **continuously** from the question’s opening until *noon UTC*, not merely hold the job at some point on December 31. The linked original question’s resolution also governs, subject to the stated annulment rules.

Probability: 87%

(a) **Time left:** About 2.7 months, from October 10 to December 31, 2026, 12:00 UTC.

(b) **Status quo:** Mourinho is Real Madrid's manager and is about two months into a three-year deal. If nothing changes, the question resolves Yes.

(c) **Reference class:** Elite-club managers in the first season of a new job, over a roughly three-month autumn window.
- In general, such managers are sacked or leave in that window maybe 5–10% of the time.
- Real Madrid under Pérez is more trigger-happy. Lopetegui was sacked in October 2018, four months in, after a 5-1 Clásico loss. Benítez went in January 2016 and Alonso in January 2026.
- Still, most Pérez appointments survive their first December.
- Mourinho has never been dismissed this early in a job. His sackings have come in his second or third season.
- Pérez staked his re-election campaign on this hire and paid Benfica €15 million to release him. That makes an early sacking costly for the president's own credibility.
- Current form is mediocre but not a crisis: 5-0-2, 4th in La Liga, no injury problems, and no reports of dressing-room or board unrest.

(d) **Scenario for No:** Madrid lose heavily at Barcelona on October 25, drop points in the league, and stumble in the Champions League group. A Vinícius or dressing-room conflict blows up, and Pérez cuts his losses in November or December, as he did with Lopetegui. A less likely route is Mourinho resigning after a clash, or leaving for health reasons.

(e) **Scenario for Yes:** Results are uneven but adequate. Madrid stay in the top four, progress in the Champions League, and Pérez's political investment buys patience at least until the January Supercopa.

(f) **Technicalities:** He must be manager continuously until noon UTC on December 31. Any break would resolve No. A sacking announced on December 30 or 31 before noon would count against him. There is no obvious ambiguity beyond that.

Probability: 89%

(a) **The time left until the outcome to the question is known:** 
Approximately 81 days and 19 hours (from October 10, 2026 to 12:00 UTC on December 31, 2026; roughly 2.7 months).

(b) **The status quo outcome if nothing changed:** 
**Yes** (Mourinho is currently the manager and under contract through June 2029).

(c) **A reference class and its base rate for events like this:** 
High-profile European managers appointed on multi-year contracts at top clubs retaining their position through December of their first season. Historically, first-season sackings within the first 6 months occur roughly 5–10% of the time across European elite clubs. Even at Real Madrid under Florentino Pérez, where managerial turnover is high, only Julen Lopetegui (sacked in late October 2018) failed to make it to December in his debut season, whereas others who struggled early (like Rafael Benítez in 2015/16) lasted at least into January. 

(d) **A brief description of a scenario that results in a No outcome:** 
Real Madrid suffers an immediate collapse over late October and November—such as dropping points to Villarreal/Sevilla, failing against RB Leipzig, and suffering a heavy, humiliating defeat away to Barcelona in El Clásico on October 25—sparking open revolt in the dressing room and prompting Florentino Pérez to fire Mourinho before the year ends (mirroring Lopetegui's 2018 dismissal).

(e) **A brief description of a scenario that results in a Yes outcome:** 
Real Madrid maintains respectable form, navigating the upcoming October/November fixtures and staying in contention in both La Liga and the Champions League. Pérez remains patient given the financial investment (€15m buyout to Benfica plus a 3-year contract) and political capital tied to Mourinho's return, keeping him in charge comfortably through the end of the calendar year.

(f) **Read the resolution criteria literally: note any technicality that could decide it:** 
The criteria require Mourinho to be manager *continuously* until 12:00 noon UTC on December 31, 2026. A temporary resignation, mutual termination, or "stepping aside" with an interim manager taking charge for even a single match before December 31 would cause the question to resolve No.

**Assessment:**
The timeframe is short (less than three months). While Real Madrid's early form is somewhat uneven (5-0-2 in La Liga), Mourinho was hired very recently with substantial financial commitment, and President Florentino Pérez personally staked his reelection campaign on this appointment. Unless results completely crater over the next several weeks—particularly in El Clásico—a mid-season sacking before January is historically very rare. Weighing the status quo, the short time horizon, and the political backing against the tail-risk of an acute crisis, the probability of him remaining in charge through December 31 is around 91%.

Probability: 91%
